releaseApproval.reviewer: Release gate review for the user-authorized v2.0.2 publication; mobile real-device acceptance delegated to the user
evidence: This release enables runtime-probed encrypted Range playback on mobile browsers with bounded caches and cancellation, and restores playback positions after foreground return. Persistent cryptographic, SQLite, backup, and client mutation contracts remain unchanged from v1.3.7.

Full local make test passed: frontend typecheck/lint/build, Go vet/tests, installer/update tests, web tests and TLS proxy tests. The final frontend error-path changes received a supplementary typecheck, complete unit suite, lint and production build; exact-commit Linux CI remains a release gate.

Local Chromium Pixel 10 emulation passed real encrypted upload and native playback/seek of a valid 257 MiB MP4 (a 3-second fixture padded with a free box), simulated hidden/visible session replacement restoring 1.2 seconds without autoplay, and idle lock erasing decrypted filenames and returning 410 for the old media URL. This does not certify content-heavy large videos or real mobile devices.

Real-device iOS Safari and Android acceptance is pending and will be performed by the user, who explicitly requested immediate v2.0.2 stable publication. Local browser emulation is not real-device certification.
Publication remains gated on successful exact-commit main CI including all-package race tests and Linux amd64/arm64 cross-builds; the release workflow checksum-publishes both architectures.

scope: XDrive v2.0.2 mobile encrypted video Range playback, bounded memory and session recovery; persistent data formats unchanged from v1.3.7

meaning.1: legacy direct Vault Key file and thumbnail derivation
meaning.2: K_data hierarchy for newly encrypted files and thumbnails

localState.plaintextPolicy: encrypted with K_local before IndexedDB persistence

sqlite.migrationPolicy: forward only; after a schema-changing migration, restore the matching pre-migration database and binary before rollback

clientMutationProtocol.acceptance: exact match only; reject missing, older, and future versions before reading mutation bodies

evolutionPolicy: Unknown payload versions and unknown fields remain fail-closed.
The listed optional fields and their absent-value meanings are part of the current schema contract.
Adding or redefining a payload field requires a new payload schema version; it must not silently expand an older strict reader.
A change that makes a stale client unsafe for mutations increments the client mutation protocol version in Go and TypeScript.
Key derivation or AAD meaning changes use their own crypto version; they do not reuse a payload schema number.
SQLite schema migration, backup container format, encrypted object envelope, and browser payload schema are independent version dimensions.
